extracted.intended_audience: readers of literary reviews, editors and authors of biographies/memoirs
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for judging and composing reminiscences, biographies, and surgical/personal memoirs — focusing on qualities like brevity, vividness, completeness, technical detail, and appropriate audience appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal information, anecdotes, and gossip
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal information, anecdotes and gossip about such people, who filled a large place in the public eye and mind, are all very fascinating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reminiscences should take the reader into the best company and supply personal detail and anecdotes — these make the work a 'mine of the deepest interest' and valuable material for early history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use representative extracts to show value
rubrics_metrics.description: The only way properly to represent the value of such a work, is to give extracts from it indicating its quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing or presenting such a volume, include representative extracts that demonstrate its character and strengths rather than only summarizing; extracts substantiate claims about interest and quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compactness and density ('compact and meaty')
rubrics_metrics.description: Few works of recent times are so compact and meaty in just those qualities which make a work valuable alike for reference and continuous perusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good biographical or reminiscence volume should be concentrated and substantial — avoid diffuseness or padding so that the work serves both as reference and for sustained reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic and picturesque brevity without diffuseness
rubrics_metrics.description: Short and well written, and the author knows how to be graphic and picturesque without being in the least diffuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for vivid, picturesque prose while remaining concise; sketches of five to fifteen pages can be fully effective if they avoid unnecessary elaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness: omit no essential fact
rubrics_metrics.description: The sketches vary from five to fifteen pages long, and are completely given, omitting no essential fact in the career, or essential trait in the character of those treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even brief biographical sketches should not sacrifice essential facts or character traits for brevity — ensure completeness of core facts and salient character details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain, simple, clear writing without pretence
rubrics_metrics.description: Language of the plainest homespun... shows a genuine mastery of the fundamental idea of good writing... simple, clear force, and luminous treatment... always without pretence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer plain, direct language and clarity over ornament; an author should avoid pretension and let clear, forceful expression carry the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include relevant professional/technical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: A large portion of the book is given to a detailed description of the various steps which he took in experimenting on vesico-vaginal fistula, and of the difficulties which he so patiently and at last so triumphantly surmounted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memoirs by practitioners should include technical descriptions of methods and experiments where appropriate — such detail increases the work's value to professionals and documents professional achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience suitability / target appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Boys will be specially interested in such a volume, and find in it both amusement and benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider and signal intended audience (e.g., youth, general readers, professionals) and craft tone, length, and content accordingly to engage that audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced moral appraisal with contextual mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: While her social errors are to be deplored, even those most downright in condemning such departures from the established order of things, when they look into all the circumstances of her life are disposed to palliate them... Certainly it must be admitted that, in spite of her deviation from that path which society so rigidly and properly exacts from woman, Mary Woolstonecraft was a person of singularly noble and pure instincts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographical criticism should weigh moral judgments against contextual circumstances, avoiding crude condemnation; aim for a balanced appraisal that recognizes faults but also mitigates them with fuller context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use anecdotes to illustrate character and reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Several very funny stories were told him by Sir Walter Scott... they well establish the reputation of this great man as a rude and unsocial bear, except when he chose to be otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and present anecdotes that concretely support character assessments (e.g., temper, manners, reputation); well-chosen stories can vividly substantiate evaluative claims.
